title: Receding Moving Object Segmentation in 3D LiDAR Data Using Sparse 4D Convolutions
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) / IROS 2022
abstract_summary: Converts sequential LiDAR scans into sparse 4D voxel representations and applies computationally efficient sparse convolutions to extract spatiotemporal features, predicting per-point moving object confidence scores. A receding horizon strategy enables online predictions that refine with new observations, while a binary Bayes filter integrates scan predictions for robust estimation. Evaluated on SemanticKITTI and Apollo datasets, relying solely on geometric point cloud information without semantic labels.

title: Moving Object Segmentation in 3D LiDAR Data: A Learning-based Approach Exploiting Sequential Data
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) / IROS 2021
abstract_summary: Presents LMNet, a learning-based method that uses sequential range image representations from rotating 3D LiDAR sensors with convolutional neural networks to distinguish moving from static objects, operating at sensor frame rates in urban settings. Distinguishes dynamic versus stationary objects without relying on semantic categories, and introduces a new evaluation benchmark derived from SemanticKITTI. Both benchmark and code are released publicly.

title: Efficient Spatial-Temporal Information Fusion for LiDAR-Based 3D Moving Object Segmentation
abstract_summary: Proposes MotionSeg3D, a dual-branch deep network that separately processes spatial and temporal information from sequential LiDAR scans using range images, then combines them with motion-guided attention modules. A point refinement module via 3D sparse convolution integrates range image and point cloud representations to reduce boundary artifacts. Achieves real-time sensor-rate processing and outperforms state-of-the-art methods on SemanticKITTI LiDAR-MOS benchmark.

title: DynamicFilter: an Online Dynamic Objects Removal Framework for Highly Dynamic Environments
abstract_summary: Presents an online removal framework for dynamic urban environments consisting of a scan-to-map front-end and a map-to-map back-end that deeply integrate visibility-based and map-based approaches. Addresses the challenge of massive dynamic objects diversifying spatial structures during robot urban navigation. Evaluated in dynamic simulation environments and real-world datasets.

title: DynaSLAM: Tracking, Mapping and Inpainting in Dynamic Scenes
abstract_summary: Builds upon ORB-SLAM2 to add dynamic object detection and background inpainting capabilities, operating across monocular, stereo, and RGB-D configurations. Detects moving objects through multi-view geometry, deep learning, or both methods, and uses a static scene map to restore frame backgrounds occluded by dynamic objects. Demonstrates superior performance over standard visual SLAM in highly dynamic environments.

title: DynaSLAM II: Tightly-Coupled Multi-Object Tracking and SLAM
abstract_summary: Extends visual SLAM to handle dynamic environments by integrating multi-object tracking using instance semantic segmentation and ORB features, jointly optimizing the static scene structure, dynamic object geometry, and trajectories of camera and moving agents through a novel bundle adjustment framework. Demonstrates that tracking moving objects enhances both scene understanding and camera localization in stereo and RGB-D configurations. Targets autonomous driving, multi-robot systems, and mixed reality applications.

title: NGD-SLAM: Towards Real-Time Dynamic SLAM without GPU
abstract_summary: Develops a CPU-exclusive visual SLAM system for dynamic environments, introducing a mask propagation mechanism that decouples camera tracking from deep learning-based masking per frame. A hybrid tracking strategy combining ORB features with optical flow methods enables selective resource allocation, achieving 60 FPS tracking on laptop CPUs while maintaining high localization accuracy in dynamic environments. First SLAM system to demonstrate feasibility of deep learning for dynamic SLAM without GPU support.

title: FAST-LIO2: Fast Direct LiDAR-inertial Odometry
abstract_summary: Presents an efficient LiDAR-inertial odometry system that registers raw point clouds directly to maps without feature extraction and employs an incremental k-d tree (ikd-Tree) for dynamic map maintenance. Achieves consistently higher accuracy at lower computational load than competing systems, operating at up to 100 Hz and supporting multiple LiDAR types. Benchmarked across 19 sequences from multiple LiDAR datasets, with code open-sourced on GitHub.

title: LeGO-LOAM: Lightweight and Ground-Optimized Lidar Odometry and Mapping on Variable Terrain
abstract_summary: Proposes a lightweight and ground-optimized lidar odometry and mapping method for real-time six degree-of-freedom pose estimation with ground vehicles, using point cloud segmentation to filter noise and feature extraction for planar and edge features. A two-step Levenberg-Marquardt optimization achieves real-time pose estimation on low-power embedded systems. Demonstrates similar or better accuracy than LOAM with reduced computational expense on variable terrain.

title: BEVFusion: Multi-Task Multi-Sensor Fusion with Unified Bird's-Eye View Representation
abstract_summary: Unifies camera and LiDAR data in a shared bird's-eye view space preserving both geometric and semantic information for multi-task multi-sensor perception. Achieves a 40x reduction in view transformation latency through optimized BEV pooling and sets new state-of-the-art on nuScenes for 3D detection and BEV map segmentation. Supports multiple 3D perception tasks with minimal architectural modifications, with code released publicly.

title: BEVFusion: A Simple and Robust LiDAR-Camera Fusion Framework
abstract_summary: Addresses the limitation of LiDAR-camera fusion methods that rely on point clouds as queries, making them inoperable when LiDAR malfunctions. Proposes a framework processing camera features independently, enabling robust detection under sensor failures and outperforming state-of-the-art by 15.7% to 28.9% mAP under simulated malfunction conditions. First method to handle realistic LiDAR malfunction without post-processing requirements.

title: Center-based 3D Object Detection and Tracking
abstract_summary: Represents 3D objects as points and detects centers using keypoint detection, then regresses 3D dimensions, orientation, and velocity, simplifying tracking to greedy closest-point matching. Achieves 65.5 NDS and 63.8 AMOTA on nuScenes and outperforms previous lidar-only methods on Waymo Open Dataset. A second-stage refinement uses additional point features to improve estimates.

title: PointPillars: Fast Encoders for Object Detection from Point Clouds
abstract_summary: Proposes PointPillars, an encoder utilizing PointNets to learn representations of point clouds organized in vertical columns (pillars), enabling fast and accurate 3D object detection running at 62 Hz for autonomous driving. Achieves significant improvements in both speed and accuracy over prior methods on KITTI benchmark, including fusion-based approaches. Designed for efficiency with minimal computational complexity.

title: Scalable Scene Flow from Point Clouds in the Real World
abstract_summary: Introduces a large-scale dataset for scene flow estimation derived from tracked 3D objects, approximately 1,000x larger than previous real-world datasets in annotated frames, and proposes FastFlow3D providing real-time inference on full point clouds. Develops human-interpretable evaluation metrics accounting for ego-motion and object-type breakdowns. Demonstrates that downsampling point clouds significantly degrades scene flow prediction performance.

title: Occupancy Flow Fields for Motion Forecasting in Autonomous Driving
abstract_summary: Introduces a spatio-temporal grid representation combining occupancy probability and 2D flow vectors per cell, bridging limitations of trajectory sets and occupancy grids for motion forecasting. Employs a deep learning architecture with a novel flow trace loss ensuring consistency between occupancy and flow predictions and introduces predicting speculative occluded agents. Evaluated on the INTERACTION dataset and proprietary autonomous driving data.

title: Social LSTM: Human Trajectory Prediction in Crowded Spaces
abstract_summary: Proposes a data-driven LSTM model with a novel social pooling layer that pools hidden representations from neighboring agents' LSTMs to capture human-human interactions for trajectory forecasting in crowded settings. Demonstrates improvements over traditional social force models, learning behaviors including collision avoidance and group movement. Foundational work establishing LSTM-based approaches for crowd trajectory prediction in shared spaces.

title: Social GAN: Socially Acceptable Trajectories with Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract_summary: Combines recurrent sequence-to-sequence models with generative adversarial networks and a novel pooling mechanism to predict multimodal, socially acceptable pedestrian trajectories in crowded environments. A variety loss encourages diverse predictions capturing the inherent multimodality of human motion. Demonstrates improvements in accuracy, variety, collision avoidance, and computational complexity over prior methods on multiple benchmark datasets.

title: AgentFormer: Agent-Aware Transformers for Socio-Temporal Multi-Agent Forecasting
abstract_summary: Proposes a Transformer architecture with an agent-aware attention mechanism that preserves agent identities, attending to elements of the same agent differently than elements of other agents, enabling direct sociotemporal feature modeling across time and agents simultaneously. Jointly models agent intents in a stochastic prediction framework where behavior uncertainty in one agent influences others. Achieves substantial improvements on pedestrian and autonomous driving trajectory forecasting benchmarks.

title: Motion Planning in Dynamic Environments Using Context-Aware Human Trajectory Prediction
abstract_summary: Integrates a context-aware human trajectory prediction method combining intention recognition with trajectory optimization-based motion planning into a full robot perception and motion planning framework, validated on a Toyota Human Support Robot using live RGB-D camera data. GPU-accelerated predicted composite distance fields significantly reduce computation time compared to traditional approaches. Releases the Oxford Indoor Human Motion dataset for indoor human trajectory research.

title: Simple Online and Realtime Tracking with a Deep Association Metric
venue: IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP 2017)
abstract_summary: Extends the SORT tracking framework by incorporating deep appearance features learned offline on a large-scale re-identification dataset, using nearest neighbor queries in visual feature space for measurement-to-track association. Reduces identity switches by 45% while maintaining real-time performance by offloading complexity to pre-training. Enables tracking through longer periods of occlusions without incurring online computational cost.

title: LV-DOT: LiDAR-visual dynamic obstacle detection and tracking for autonomous robot navigation
abstract_summary: Presents a LiDAR-camera fusion framework that integrates outputs from multiple low-accuracy but computationally efficient detectors to avoid the demands of sophisticated 3D detection systems for indoor robot navigation. Employs tracking through feature-based association and Kalman filtering, with a dynamic obstacle classification algorithm for identifying moving objects. Validated on datasets and physical quadcopter experiments, outperforming benchmarks across IoU thresholds.

title: Moving Object Segmentation in Point Cloud Data using Hidden Markov Models
venue: IROS 2024 Workshop on Long-Term Perception for Autonomy in Dynamic Human-shared Environments
abstract_summary: Presents a learning-free method using hidden Markov models to segment dynamic objects in point cloud data, modeling individual voxels with HMMs and integrating probabilistic beliefs into maps through HMM filtering. Performs competitively with deep learning approaches on benchmark datasets while maintaining strong generalization across different sensor types and environments. Provides publicly available code.

title: Deep Person Detection in 2D Range Data
abstract_summary: Extends the DROW wheelchair and walker detector to general person detection using 2D laser range data from mobile robots, incorporating temporal information through a short online window in the network architecture. Expands the DROW dataset with person annotations, creating the largest dataset of person annotations in 2D range data collected in real-world environments. Demonstrates superior performance over three baseline methods, addressing occlusion, dynamic leg motion, and crowding.

title: Deep Learning-Based Object Detection, Localisation and Tracking for Smart Wheelchair Healthcare Mobility
venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract_summary: Presents a perception system for autonomous wheelchairs adapting YOLOv3 for object detection, integrating depth estimation using an Intel RealSense camera, and implementing SORT-based tracking for indoor navigation-relevant objects such as doors and door handles. Achieves 3.8% average depth estimation error and 90% precision for door detection with the pipeline running at 5.8 FPS on embedded hardware. Validated in a controlled laboratory environment using a Vicon motion capture system.

title: Real-time open-vocabulary perception for mobile robots on edge devices: a systematic analysis of the accuracy-latency trade-off
abstract_summary: Provides a systematic analysis of optimization trade-offs for real-time open-vocabulary robotic perception on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, evaluating combinations of detection models (NanoOWL, YOLO-World) with segmentation models (NanoSAM, EfficientViT-SAM) optimized via TensorRT at FP32, FP16, and INT8 precision. Quantitatively compares mIoU and latency for each pipeline configuration, offering practical insights for deploying Vision-Language Models on edge hardware for human-robot interaction.

title: Benchmarking YOLOv8 Variants for Object Detection Efficiency on Jetson Orin NX for Edge Computing Applications
abstract_summary: Benchmarks YOLOv8 model variants on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX platform evaluating inference latency, frame throughput, and computational resource usage across varying input sizes and model complexities. TensorRT outperforms PyTorch by 17.7% at batch size 2, with YOLOv8n achieving 52 FPS and 65 FPS with INT8 quantization. Energy consumption for Jetson Orin NX ranges from 10 to 14 W, providing practical guidance for wheelchair-scale edge deployments.

title: CoNav Chair: Design of a ROS-based Smart Wheelchair for Shared Control Navigation in the Built Environment
abstract_summary: Develops a ROS-based smart wheelchair platform using a shared control navigation algorithm and obstacle avoidance to support people with disabilities while maintaining user autonomy in indoor social environments. Emphasizes trust and autonomy for acceptance of assistive mobility technologies in the built environment, bridging the gap between full autonomy and manual control. Provides a reference architecture for wheelchair shared autonomy systems.
